turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I was wondering if you could tell me what brought you in.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sure, um, I have been coughing a lot. I've been feeling short of breath and I just feel really wheezy, so I thought I should come check it out.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, when did the cough start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've always had a cough. Well, I guess I've had a cough for the past five years, but over the past three days it's gotten a lot worse.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, did anything happen 3 days ago that has brought the cough on?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, I was, I did groceries, I came home and then I started coughing a little bit more and I haven't been able to stop since.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, is there any particular time of day that the cough is worse, like morning, night?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, it seems to be worse in the morning.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you bringing up any sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I am. Umm, and it looks yellow and sometimes even green.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. With your cough prior to three days ago were you bringing up sputum with that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I guess some, but it was clear.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you bringing up more sputum now, the same or less?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, more sputum, and sputum just looks different.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you noticed any blood?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and you mentioned you've been you've had a wheeze, when you do you notice that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I also, I guess I notice that mostly last night, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um and what types of activities have you had shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I guess walking, doing day to day things has made me feel a little bit more short of breath than I used to feel.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you been experiencing any other symptoms besides the cough, wheeze and shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I feel a little bit more tired, but other than that, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So a bit more tired. How has your sleep been?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: My sleep has been, um, pretty normal. It's been, yeah, it's been the same. I guess it's the coughing that's making me tired.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had any ear pain or eye pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ear pain, or eye pain? No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any discharge from either, either your ears or eyes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you had a runny nose?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Or felt congested?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had a sore throat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Or any difficulty swallowing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Changes to your sense of smell or taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had any changes in appetite?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and have you had any weight loss over the last several months?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Weight loss, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. How about have you had any fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Fevers or chills ah, no. No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Nights, how about night sweats?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you had any chest pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ah no, no chest. Well my chest feels, I guess sometimes I, it feels painful because I'm coughing so much, but nothing more than that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you get chest pain when you exert yourself physically?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so it's just after the coughing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and how would you describe the character of the chest pain? Some people will say sharp, dull, achy.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I would say dull.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you had any like heart palpitations, feeling like your heart's racing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how about any episodes where you felt like you were going to faint or, yeah, pass out?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uhm and have you had any swelling in your feet, ankles, hands?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And then have you had any urinary problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any bowel problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and then any joint pains or muscle aches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how about any rashes anywhere?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and then, sorry, have you had any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. In terms of your past medical history, have you been diagnosed with any conditions before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I have high blood pressure and diabetes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see. Are you on any medications for those?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, for the blood pressure, the high blood pressure, I'm on a beta blocker and then for my diabetes I'm on metformin.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uh, do you, are you taking any other medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, just some calcium and vitamin D.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any surgeries in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any allergies to medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Are your immunizations up to date?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I believe so, but I recently learned that I should get something called the pneumococcal vaccine. I haven't gotten that yet.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, you're you're right. So for um, in Canada or anybody or in Ontario, at least, anybody who's older than 65, it's recommended to get this vaccine to protect against certain types of bacterial infections type which can cause pneumonia. So it would be good something that you can set up with your family doctor.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, and so are you, so do you smoke cigarettes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I used to.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how much do you smoke or how much did you use to smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I smoked a pack a day and I smoked for 45 years, but I stopped two years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, that's great that you were able to stop. Do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, occasionally like once every two weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any triggers that you can think of you were exposed to either at work or home like chemicals or things that you were exposed to that you had to breathe, that you breathe in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you traveled anywhere?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and have you been near anybody who's been sick or has similar symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and anybody in the family have a heart or lung condition?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any cancers in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, there was a liver cancer.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and, I think that.. OK, and that was all I wanted to ask on history. Was there anything else that you wanted to tell me today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, just um, what do you think the problem is? I've never felt this bad with my shortness of breath before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, certainly so umm, it, it sounds like it could be maybe a viral infection that I brought on this cough and worsen the sputum. This could be a bacterial infection, it could be a COPD exacerbation and also one of the other things that we would have to consider right now is Covid as well and so we will do a PCR nasal swab for Covid and a chest Xx-ray and some other investigations as well and uhm, we will try to get to the bottom of what's causing your your shortness of breath.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, that sounds good, thank you.
